tickets.subject: JWT Migration Breaking Our Integration

conversation.message: We've been using API keys since v2.0 and now getting 401 errors after the upgrade. Our keys are still listed in the dashboard. The migration docs don't explain how to transition. We have 47 microservices using the old auth method.
API keys were deprecated in v2.1. You'll need to switch to JWT authentication. I've sent the auth endpoint details.

We understand JWT is the new method, but we need a transition period. Can we use both during migration? Some services are harder to update than others. Also, the /me/api-keys endpoint still works - does that mean keys are still valid?
Escalating to documentation team. We need clearer migration guidance for enterprise customers with complex deployments.

tickets.internal_notes: Customer has valid point - we deprecated but didn't remove. Docs should clarify the transition period and when keys will be fully removed (v3). Also need to document the parallel auth support during migration window.

tickets.subject: Webhook Not Firing for Deleted Datasets

conversation.message: We set up webhooks for all events including dataset.deleted but never receive callbacks when datasets are archived. Is this a bug or expected behavior?
Can you share your webhook configuration? I'll check what events you have subscribed to.

Here's our config: {"url": "https://hooks.datapipe.io/datasync", "events": ["dataset.created", "dataset.updated", "dataset.deleted", "sync.completed", "sync.failed"]}. We're getting callbacks for created and updated, but not deleted.

I checked with engineering. The 'dataset.deleted' event isn't currently implemented - DELETE /datasets/{id} does a soft delete (archive) which triggers dataset.updated. Escalating for documentation clarification.

tickets.internal_notes: Webhook events list in docs may be incomplete or misleading. Customer assumed dataset.deleted exists based on naming convention. Need to clarify: 1) what events actually exist, 2) that DELETE is soft-delete triggering 'updated' event, 3) whether dataset.deleted is planned.

tickets.subject: Rate Limiting Inconsistent Between Endpoints

conversation.message: We're hitting rate limits way faster on bulk record inserts than on regular GET requests. The docs say 100 req/min for free tier but we can do maybe 20 bulk inserts before getting 429. Is there separate rate limiting for different endpoint types?
Good question. Let me check with the engineering team about rate limit categories.
Engineering confirmed: bulk endpoints have a separate 'bulk' rate limit category with lower limits. Free tier is 20 bulk requests/min. This isn't documented anywhere. Escalating.
That explains it. Where can we find the full rate limit breakdown? We need to design our sync jobs around these limits.

tickets.internal_notes: Rate limit categories (standard, bulk, sync) are in the CSV but not explained in user-facing docs. Need comprehensive rate limit documentation including: per-category limits, how categories map to endpoints, headers returned, and retry strategies.

documentation_gaps_identified: JWT migration path for existing API key users
Complete webhook event list with soft-delete behavior
Rate limit categories and per-category limits by tier
